title: Email6 IMAP connection-attempt recovery and provider-retry index: database evidence

sources.note: statement hashes are sha256 of the exact SQL text inside the Rust source; c0 is an unpublished diagnostic recovery draft; c1/c3 are its final key-fenced/indexed query shapes. The draft was never deployed.

measuredSchemaBeforeForwardMigrationRevi.note: The original diagnostic schema assembled lease fields and the CASE index in the attempt CREATE TABLE. The final forward migrations preserve the original applied table migration and produce the same lease columns and CASE index under the new due index name. Business SQL is unchanged; current named-index plans and upgrade rehearsal are separate checks.

method.engine: PostgreSQL 14, local disposable databases, one per dataset, dropped after measurement

statistics.fresh: VACUUM ANALYZE after seeding (and after each case setup)
statistics.stale: ANALYZE after the first 20 rows (attempts) or a small first seed phase (streams), autovacuum off, then the rest seeded

method.isolation: every measured statement runs inside a transaction that is rolled back; writes are pg_stat_xact deltas
method.measure: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS); buffers = shared hit + read of the top plan node
method.syntheticData: synthetic links/streams/folders: 4% of IMAP streams with future provider waits; two hot links with 5,010 streams each; ordinary links with 10 streams; plus a completed-wait population (about half of the remaining streams of every provider get a past provider_retry_at)
method.notClaimed: no throughput, latency, production or tracing claims; timings are omitted on purpose

reportingBudget.scope: Final candidate attempt-matrix statements only; diagnostic-draft and without-index controls intentionally exceed this budget. Not an RPC, recovery-cycle or production capacity guarantee.

findings: c3 attempt matrix: 48 cases x 2 plan modes = 96 runs at 1k/10k/100k attempts, fresh and stale statistics; no sequential scan on the attempt table in any statement.

Same-data initial-draft vs final-query comparison (stale statistics, 4 cases x 3 sizes = 12 cases): lease/defer/abandon/claim drop from up to 91,566 / 50,222 buffers to tens; c0 scales with table size, c1 does not.

Claim worst case 813-817 buffers at 100k appears only in empty_none_pending under the custom plan (generic: 8) and equals c0; it is index churn left by restoring the previous case, not growth with pending rows. locked_head_200 (another session holds 200 due heads) reads 625-628 and still claims one row.

Retry index, original provider_retry statement unchanged, 48 cells: identical results to a direct scoped max in every cell; the stale custom plan goes from a sequential scan (34,090 buffers) to an index-only scan (203).

Plan shape nuance: custom plans and stale generic plans use Index Only Scan Backward + Limit; the fresh generic plan uses a forward Index Only Scan + Aggregate. Both carry Index Cond (link_id, generation, provider_retry_at > now()), so the read is bounded by the link/generation future-wait range.

The ~203-206 buffer hot-link cells with the index are heap visibility checks of the ~200 future waits that the test itself moved inside its uncommitted transaction (dead index entries); ordinary links read 3-5 buffers.
Attempt-matrix provider-retry outlier: the 1k stale generic deferred-heavy case reads 203 buffers through the bounded retry index; the 100k maximum is 5 buffers. No sequential scan.
Sibling control (lifecycle resync max with folder role join): see siblingControl; results match an independent scoped max in every cell, with and without the index.

CREATE INDEX email_imap_connection_attempts_pending
    ON email_imap_connection_attempts (
        (CASE WHEN completed THEN 'infinity'::timestamptz
            ELSE GREATEST(recovery_at, COALESCE(lease_until, '-infinity'::timestamptz))
        END), id
    ) WHERE (CASE WHEN completed THEN 'infinity'::timestamptz
        ELSE GREATEST(recovery_at, COALESCE(lease_until, '-infinity'::timestamptz))
    END) < 'infinity'::timestamptz;
